report:
Reviewed the complete schedule_independence claim, ordinary merge.rs implementation entry, explicit semantic_spec.rs TODO implementation entry, and both associated tests. The guarantee holds semantic inputs and configured limits fixed. Its required invariant fields are answer class, output, substitutions, residuals, hints, response numbering, ambiguity versus overflow, and overflow kind. Discovery, cancellation timing, trace order, elapsed work, and memory consumption are explicitly permitted to vary.

Implemented evidence establishes a limited completed-candidate reduction slice. merge_candidate_results sorts and deduplicates candidates before decisions, selects an unconditional Proven answer with empty substitution and trivially true residual, returns a single surviving definite/ambiguous candidate or No for exhausted complete negatives, and otherwise routes to hint merging. The sorted iteration also gives a stable tie break in non_dominated_yes. This is not a claim that the whole asynchronous solver or configured resource accounting is schedule-independent. Captured goal helpers show true_ constructs an empty conjunction and is_trivially_true recognizes exactly that shape; captured result definitions distinguish Proven/Type output, substitutions, modulo residuals, response binders and Maybe hints, but do not provide the promised distinct overflow taxonomy.

The complete ordinary test final_answer_rules_are_order_independent constructs the same No, empty-hint Maybe and unconditional Yes values in three candidate orders and asserts equality to the entire unconditional stashed result. This detects a first-completed No/Maybe winning over the same available unconditional proof. Its additional duplicate-Maybe and duplicate-No assertions check their answer classes. Setup helpers in merge.rs construct genuinely empty binders/substitutions/hints and a true residual. These assertions substantiate the ordinary reduction subset; they do not exercise nonempty output/substitution/residual/hint values, response renumbering, real ready-queue perturbations, resource exhaustion, or overflow distinctions.

Those remaining obligations are honestly covered by existing explicit TODO evidence, not by assertions. The TODO implementation says deterministic resource accounting and scheduler perturbation guarantees remain planned, and solver_schedule_independence specifies a perturbed-ready-queue matrix across proof, normalization, residual, ambiguity and every overflow case, requiring byte-identical stashed results except nonsemantic traces. Completion requires deterministic resource accounting and overflow classification plus controllable scheduler perturbation, then fixtures exercising all the listed nonempty result fields and response numbering with fixed limits. Until then cancellation/discovery timing and permitted work/memory changes cannot be taken as demonstrated to leave semantic results unchanged. This deferral is accepted as visible partial implementation and test coverage, not approval of end-to-end scheduling independence. The empty TODO test supplies no behavioral evidence. No N/A entries exist.

Execution: the first cargo test -p sage-ir final_answer_rules_are_order_independent -- --exact invocation matched zero tests and is not evidence. The corrected cargo test -p sage-ir check::solve::merge::tests::final_answer_rules_are_order_independent -- --exact executed one test and passed (70 filtered); existing compiler warnings were emitted. No production or test source was modified. Additional context was captured using review read; no broader solver claims are inferred from uninspected helpers or passing placeholders.
